title: Anatomy of a Claude Code session
dek: A Claude Code session is a conversation file named by a UUID, and the process you talk to is only a lease on it. This is a teardown of Claude Code 2.1.280 for building an OS around it: what a session is made of and where each part lives on disk, all 120 command-line options (57 of them hidden), the global state file every process rewrites, the stream-json and control protocol a host uses to drive a session, the six other ways into a running one, the ways Claude hands work to other programs, and the friction map for an OS that owns what the process forgets.
byline: 24 September 2026 · Subject: Claude Code 2.1.280 (desktop build, macOS arm64)
description: A teardown of Claude Code 2.1.280 sessions: identity, boot, the turn loop, the on-disk layout, the transcript graph, all 120 CLI options, settings and environment, the ~/.claude.json state file, permissions, the stream-json control protocol, the Agent SDK, the other doors into a session, offloading work to apps, and what an OS should own.
og_description: What a Claude Code session is made of, measured on one machine and read from the 2.1.280 binary: four identities, nine boot steps, the transcript graph, 120 options, the state file every process rewrites, 66 control requests, seven doors, and the friction map for building an OS around it.
twitter_description: Claude Code 2.1.280 taken apart for an OS: the conversation is the only durable object, the process is a lease, and every flag, file and protocol message sits around them.
